question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

As he is not satisfied / with the jury's decision, / he appeal / in the higher court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. he appeal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "He" is a third person singular subject, so in the simple present tense the verb must take "-s" → "he appeals".

◦ Correct: As he is not satisfied with the jury's decision, he appeals in the higher court.

• The main clause is in the present tense (matching "is not satisfied"), so the verb should also be present, giving "appeals".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "as he is not satisfied", "with the jury's decision" and "in the higher court" are all correct.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement (simple present): singular subject (he/she/it) + verb-s (he appeals); plural subject (they/we) + base verb (they appeal).

• Remember: only ONE "-s" rule — either the subject is plural OR the verb has "-s", never both.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

He received an honarary degree for his contributions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Honorary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Honorary", meaning given as an honour, without the usual requirements or payment. (मानद / सम्मानार्थ)

◦ Example: The university conferred an honorary doctorate on the scientist.

• Spelling key: HON + OR + ARY — single "n", "-orary" ending.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Honnary", 3 "Honnaary" and 4 "Honnorary" are all misspellings (they wrongly double the "n").

NOTE

• Related words: honour, honourable, honorary, honorarium (a token payment). Note that "honorary" and "honorarium" drop the "u" of "honour".

question: Select the option that has an error in the usage of the present perfect tense.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ravi has complete his homework.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect tense is formed as has/have + past participle (V3). The past participle of "complete" is "completed", not "complete". Hence it must be "Ravi has completed his homework."

◦ Correct: Ravi has completed his homework.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 correctly use "have/has + completed" (the proper past participle).

NOTE

• Present perfect (has/have + V3) connects a past action to the present. Common time markers: already, just, yet, recently, so far, ever, never.

• Do not confuse the base form (complete) with the past participle (completed) after has/have.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mischievious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mischievious" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Mischievous", meaning playfully troublesome or naughty. (शरारती)

◦ Example: The mischievous child hid his sister's shoes.

• Spelling key: MIS + CHIE + VOUS — there is no extra "i" before "-ous" (it is "-vous", not "-vious").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Occurred" (double "r", double "c"), "Questionnaire" (double "n") and "Peculiar" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly mispronounced/misspelt: mischievous (not "mischievious"), grievous (not "grievious"), mischief. Watch out for the wrong extra "i".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Skeleton in the cupboard
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An embarrassing and hidden fact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "skeleton in the cupboard" (or "skeleton in the closet") means a shocking, shameful or embarrassing secret that is kept hidden. (छिपा हुआ शर्मनाक रहस्य)

◦ Example: Every family has a skeleton in the cupboard that they prefer not to discuss.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 miss the key idea of the secret being hidden AND embarrassing/shameful.

NOTE

• Related idioms of secrecy: "let the cat out of the bag" (reveal a secret), "under wraps" (kept secret), "an open secret" (widely known but officially unacknowledged).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

I regret / in notify that / the model you want / is out of stock.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in notify that.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the verb "regret", when it is followed by another verb of announcing, we use the to-infinitive — "regret to notify/inform/say". Hence "in notify" should be "to notify".

◦ Correct: I regret to notify that the model you want is out of stock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "I regret", "the model you want" and "is out of stock" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Regret + to + verb" is used for present/future bad news (I regret to inform you...). "Regret + verb-ing" refers to being sorry about a past action (I regret telling him). The two structures have different meanings.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Through thick and thin
option_1: To pass through thick and thin air
option_2: To be supportive in both good and bad times
option_3: To possess both thick and thin clothes
option_4: To travel through thick and thin clouds
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To be supportive in both good and bad times.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "through thick and thin" means through both good and bad times; under all circumstances, remaining loyal and supportive. (हर परिस्थिति में / सुख-दुख में साथ)

◦ Example: A true friend stands by you through thick and thin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 take the idiom literally (air, clothes, clouds) and miss its figurative meaning of steadfast support.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of loyalty/support: "stand by someone", "come rain or shine", "through the ups and downs".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sculpter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sculpter" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Sculptor", meaning an artist who makes sculptures (statues/figures). (मूर्तिकार)

◦ Example: The sculptor carved a beautiful statue out of marble.

• Spelling key: SCULP + TOR — the ending is "-or", not "-er".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Pursuit", "Almighty" and "Stampede" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: sculpt (verb), sculpture (the artwork), sculptor (the artist). Many "doer" nouns end in "-or": actor, doctor, editor, sculptor, inventor, director.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

When Shina reached the bus stand, she realised that she has left her wallet at home.
option_4: she had been left her wallet
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. she had left her wallet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two past actions occur, the earlier action takes the past perfect (had + V3) and the later action takes the simple past. Leaving the wallet happened before she reached the bus stand, so it needs the past perfect — "she had left her wallet".

◦ Correct: When Shina reached the bus stand, she realised that she had left her wallet at home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because "has left" (present perfect) clashes with the past-tense context.

• Option 3 "leaves" (present) is wrong tense.

• Option 4 "had been left" is a wrong passive construction.

NOTE

• Rule: In a sentence with two past events, use past perfect (had + V3) for the one that happened first, and simple past for the one that happened later.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: He is famous for all his contributions for weekly magazines.
option_2: He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.
option_3: He is more famous for all his contributions for weekly magazines.
option_4: He is more famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "contribution" collocates with the preposition "to" (a contribution to something), not "for". Hence "contributions to weekly magazines".

• The adjective "famous" here needs no comparative ("more famous") because no comparison with another person is being made.

◦ Correct: He is famous for all his contributions to weekly magazines.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 3 use the wrong preposition "for" after "contributions".

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly add "more" (comparative) with no "than" comparison.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "famous for" (a quality/work), "contribution to" (a cause/field), "contribute to" something.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The corporator gathered heaps of curses, and his misdeeds can never be forgiven by the people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Transgressions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Misdeeds" means wrongful or wicked acts; offences. Its closest synonym is "transgressions" — violations of law, duty or moral principle. (कुकर्म / अपराध)

◦ Example: The leader's misdeeds/transgressions cost him public trust.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Consequences" (results), Option 2 "Arguments" (disputes) and Option 4 "Confrontation" (a hostile encounter) do not mean wrongful acts.

NOTE

• Synonyms of misdeed: transgression, wrongdoing, offence, crime, sin, misconduct.

• "Transgress" (verb) = to go beyond a limit / to break a law or moral code.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

It is a betterment of his work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Worsening.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Betterment" means an improvement or the act of making something better. Its antonym is "worsening", meaning becoming worse or deteriorating. (सुधार का विलोम — बिगड़ना)

◦ Example: The reforms aimed at the betterment of the poor, but poor planning led to a worsening of their condition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Growth" and Option 3 "Improvement" are synonyms of betterment.

• Option 1 "Popularity" is unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of betterment: improvement, enhancement, upliftment, amelioration.

• Antonyms: worsening, deterioration, decline, degradation.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Sarah said that she hates it when people ______ at her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. stare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stare" means to look fixedly at someone or something for a long time. It fits the context and takes the preposition "at" — "when people stare at her". (घूरना)

◦ Example: It is rude to stare at strangers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "star" (a celestial body / to feature) and Option 4 "stair" (a step) are unrelated homophones.

• Option 3 "steer" (to guide/drive) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Beware of homophones: stare (to gaze) / stair (a step); star (in the sky) / steer (to guide). Only "stare at" fits the sense of looking fixedly.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Mary appeared for the test. She was waiting anxiously for the test result.
option_2: hitting the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on pins and needles.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on pins and needles" means in a state of anxious anticipation or nervous suspense. It exactly replaces "waiting anxiously". (बेचैनी/उत्सुकता से प्रतीक्षा करना)

◦ Example: She was on pins and needles while waiting for the interview call.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a piece of cake" — something very easy.

• Option 2 "hitting the nail on the head" — describing something exactly right.

• Option 4 "jumping through hoops" — doing many difficult things to achieve something.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of anxiety/suspense: "on tenterhooks", "on edge", "with bated breath", "biting one's nails".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

A medicine to counteract the effect of another medicine
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Antidote.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "antidote" is a medicine or remedy taken to counteract the effects of a poison or another substance/medicine. (विषहर / प्रतिविष औषधि)

◦ Example: The doctor administered an antidote to neutralise the snake venom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Alimony" — money paid to a spouse after divorce/separation.

• Option 2 "Antibiotic" — a medicine that kills or stops the growth of bacteria.

• Option 4 "Anticoagulant" — a substance that prevents the clotting of blood.

NOTE

• Useful "anti-" (against) words: antidote (against poison), antibiotic (against bacteria), antiseptic (against germs), antibody, antacid (against acidity).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains grammatical error(s).

At the zoo, a curious child / fed an elephant some peanuts, / while enthusiastic group of the visitors / watched in amazement.
option_1: At the zoo, a curious child
option_2: while enthusiastic group of the visitors
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. while enthusiastic group of the visitors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A singular countable noun ("group") needs an article. The phrase should read "while an enthusiastic group of the visitors".

◦ Correct: ... while an enthusiastic group of the visitors watched in amazement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "At the zoo, a curious child", "fed an elephant some peanuts" and "watched in amazement" are all correct.

NOTE

• Countable singular nouns require a determiner (a/an/the/my/this). Use "an" before a vowel sound — "an enthusiastic group", "an hour", "an honest man".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Contaminate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pollute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contaminate" means to make something impure or dirty by adding a harmful or polluting substance. Its closest synonym is "pollute". (दूषित करना / प्रदूषित करना)

◦ Example: Factory waste can contaminate/pollute river water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Clean" and 2 "purify" are antonyms of contaminate.

• Option 3 "Excel" (to be outstanding) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of contaminate: pollute, taint, infect, defile, adulterate.

• Antonyms: purify, clean, decontaminate, sterilise.

question: From the given options, identify the sentence which is in the positive degree.
option_1: I have a greater idea in this regard.
option_2: His brother is an intelligent boy.
option_3: She is the most beautiful girl of the class.
option_4: They are playing hockey with longer sticks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. His brother is an intelligent boy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The positive degree uses the base (simple) form of an adjective with no comparison — here "intelligent" is used plainly to describe the boy.

◦ "His brother is an intelligent boy" — positive degree.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "greater" and Option 4 "longer" are in the comparative degree.

• Option 3 "the most beautiful" is in the superlative degree.

NOTE

• Three degrees of comparison: Positive (tall), Comparative (taller, used with "than"), Superlative (tallest, used with "the"). The positive degree simply describes without comparing.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The ambiguous statement of the leader raised criticism among the public.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Clear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambiguous" means having more than one possible meaning; unclear or open to interpretation. Its antonym is "clear" — easy to understand and unambiguous. (अस्पष्ट का विलोम — स्पष्ट)

◦ Example: The instructions were so ambiguous that no one knew what to do; a clear set of steps would have helped.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Confusing" and Option 4 "Puzzled" are close in sense to ambiguous, not opposite.

• Option 2 "Disorganised" (lacking order) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ambiguous: vague, unclear, equivocal, obscure.

• Antonyms: clear, explicit, unambiguous, definite, lucid.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

From contacting our loved ones to buying groceries for our daily needs, mobile phones fulfilled our every requirement during the COVID-19 pandemic. Not only during the pandemic, but mobile phones have also _______ our needs since the time of their invention.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. served.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Served" means fulfilled a need or was useful for a purpose. It fits the positive context of mobile phones meeting our needs. (सेवा की / उपयोगी रहा)

◦ Example: This old car has served us well for ten years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "exasperated" (greatly irritated), Option 3 "annoyed" (irritated) and Option 4 "incensed" (made very angry) all carry a negative sense that contradicts the positive tone of the passage.

NOTE

• "Serve" collocations: serve a purpose, serve one's needs, serve the nation, serve customers. Here it means to be useful and meet requirements.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the auxiliary "had", so it needs the past participle (V3) to form the past perfect tense — "had gone". (go – went – gone)

◦ Correct: My parents and younger sister had gone to my uncle's house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "went" is the simple past (V2) and cannot follow "had".

• Option 3 "go" (base form) and Option 4 "going" (-ing form) do not fit after "had".

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3). The verb "go" forms: go (V1) – went (V2) – gone (V3).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. spend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the to-infinitive marker "to" (expressing purpose) — "to my uncle's house to spend the day". After "to", we use the base form of the verb. (दिन बिताने के लिए)

◦ Correct: ... had gone to my uncle's house to spend the day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spent" (past), Option 3 "spends" (present -s) and Option 4 "spending" (-ing) cannot follow the infinitive "to".

NOTE

• The infinitive of purpose (to + base verb) explains why something is done: "She went to the market to buy vegetables".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage narrates a past event ("At 5:00 p.m, someone ___ the door bell"), so the simple past tense is needed. The simple past of "ring" is "rang". (ring – rang – rung)

◦ Correct: At 5:00 p.m, someone rang the door bell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ring" (base) and Option 2 "rings" (present -s) are present tense.

• Option 4 "rung" is the past participle (V3), which needs "has/have/had" before it.

NOTE

• Verb forms: ring (V1) – rang (V2) – rung (V3). Use V2 (rang) for a simple past action; use V3 (rung) only with has/have/had.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Mr. Sinha" is third person singular, and the sentence is in the past continuous tense ("was + standing"). Hence the correct auxiliary is "was". (एकवचन कर्ता → was)

◦ Correct: Mr. Sinha was standing with his suitcase.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "were" is used with plural subjects (they/we/you), not the singular "Mr. Sinha".

• Option 4 "is" (present) breaks the past-tense narration; Option 3 "been" needs "has/have/had" before it.

NOTE

• Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing. Use "was" with I/he/she/it (singular) and "were" with you/we/they (plural).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was Saturday evening last week. My parents and younger sister had (1)_______ to my uncle's house to (2)_______ the day. I had stayed back to prepare for a class test. At 5:00 p.m, someone (3)_____ the door bell. To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha (4)______ standing with his suitcase. I had to call him in most unwillingly. He was a big bore and nothing less than a chatterbox. I asked his preference (5)____ coffee and tea.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. between.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Between" is used when referring to two things or people. Since the choice is among two items (coffee and tea), "between" is correct — "his preference between coffee and tea". (दो के बीच)

◦ Correct: I asked his preference between coffee and tea.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "among" is used for more than two things.

• Options 3 "on" and 4 "around" do not fit the sense of choosing between two options.

NOTE

• Rule: between → two persons/things (between you and me); among → more than two (among the students). This between/among distinction is a favourite SSC topic.

question: As per National Multidimensional Poverty Index report 2023, what is the poverty rate of India (2019-21)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.96%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report 2023, released by NITI Aayog, about 14.96% of India's population was multidimensionally poor in 2019–21. (बहुआयामी गरीबी दर — 14.96%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The report noted that around 13.5 crore people moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2015–16 and 2019–21.

• India's national MPI uses three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — measured through 12 indicators, based on the global methodology of OPHI and UNDP.

NOTE

• A person is "multidimensionally poor" if deprived in at least one-third (weighted) of the indicators. Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh had the highest poverty rates.

question: Which of the following groups of plants are categorised as cryptogams?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bryophytes and Thallophyta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cryptogams" are non-flowering, non-seed-bearing plants that reproduce by spores and have hidden/inconspicuous reproductive organs. They include Thallophyta (algae, fungi), Bryophyta (mosses, liverworts) and Pteridophyta (ferns). (क्रिप्टोगैम्स — बीजरहित पौधे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The plant kingdom is broadly divided into Cryptogams (seedless: Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta) and Phanerogams (seed-bearing: Gymnosperms and Angiosperms).

• Bryophytes are called the "amphibians of the plant kingdom".

NOTE

• "Cryptogamae" means "hidden reproduction" (crypto = hidden, gamos = marriage). "Phanerogamae" (phaneros = visible) are the seed plants with visible reproductive structures (flowers/cones).

question: Which physical feature of India is known for its lateritic soil which supports plantation crops?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Western Ghats.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Western Ghats are known for their lateritic soil, which is well-suited to plantation crops such as tea, coffee, rubber, cashew and spices. (पश्चिमी घाट — लैटेराइट मृदा)

• Laterite soil forms in areas of high temperature and heavy rainfall with alternate wet and dry seasons (leaching of silica).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lateritic soils are rich in iron and aluminium but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter; they are reddish due to iron oxide.

• Such soils are also found in the Eastern Ghats, parts of Odisha, Assam and the hills of Karnataka and Kerala.

NOTE

• Major soil types of India: Alluvial (most fertile, Northern Plains), Black/Regur (cotton, Deccan Trap), Red (Deccan), Laterite (plantation crops) and Desert/Arid soils.

question: Select the correct order of the following metals in terms of their increasing reactivities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Au, Cu, Mg and K.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the reactivity (activity) series, metals are arranged from most reactive to least reactive. Among these four, the increasing order of reactivity is: Au (gold, least reactive) < Cu (copper) < Mg (magnesium) < K (potassium, most reactive). (सक्रियता श्रेणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A common reactivity series (most → least reactive): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au.

• Potassium (K) reacts vigorously even with cold water, while gold (Au) is a noble metal that does not react with air, water or most acids.

NOTE

• More reactive metals can displace less reactive metals from their salt solutions (e.g., iron displaces copper from copper sulphate). Gold and platinum lie at the bottom (least reactive).

question:
Match the following and choose the correct option:

1. Multi-Party System – a) USA   2. Two Party system – b) China   3. Single Party system – c) India
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 - c, 2 - a, 3 - b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of party systems with countries is:

◦ 1. Multi-Party System → c) India — many parties compete, and governments are often coalitions.

◦ 2. Two-Party System → a) USA — dominated mainly by two parties (Democrats and Republicans).

◦ 3. Single-Party System → b) China — one party (the Communist Party of China) holds power.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4 (1-c, 2-a, 3-b).

Additional Information

• In a multi-party system (India, France), several parties have a real chance of gaining power, often leading to coalition governments.

• In a two-party system (USA, UK broadly), two major parties dominate.

• In a one-party system (China, North Korea), only one party is legally allowed to govern.

NOTE

• India is the world's largest democracy, with a multi-party parliamentary system based on universal adult franchise.

question: Who among the following assumed the position of Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) in May 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Praveen Kumar Srivastava.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Praveen Kumar Srivastava assumed office as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) in May 2023. (केंद्रीय सतर्कता आयुक्त — प्रवीण कुमार श्रीवास्तव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is the apex anti-corruption body of India, set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee. It became a statutory body through the CVC Act, 2003.

• The CVC consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner (Chairperson) and up to two Vigilance Commissioners, appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee (PM, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition).

NOTE

• The CVC oversees vigilance in central government organisations; the CBI takes instructions from the CVC in corruption cases. It submits its annual report to the President.

question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index of India: A Progress Review 2023, which of the following states has the LOWEST percentage of population being multidimensionally poor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National MPI: A Progress Review 2023 (NITI Aayog), Sikkim had one of the lowest percentages of multidimensionally poor population among the listed states. (सिक्किम — न्यूनतम बहुआयामी गरीबी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• States/UTs with very low multidimensional poverty include Kerala, Goa, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu and UTs like Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Chandigarh, Delhi.

• States with the highest multidimensional poverty are Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh.

NOTE

• The MPI captures deprivation across Health, Education and Standard of Living (12 indicators). Lower MPI reflects better access to nutrition, schooling, sanitation, electricity, housing, etc.

question: In which year was the Shri Mahila SEWA Sahakari Bank established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1974.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Shri Mahila SEWA Sahakari Bank (a cooperative bank of the Self-Employed Women's Association) was established in 1974 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. It was one of the first women's cooperative banks in India, promoting financial inclusion for poor self-employed women. (श्री महिला सेवा सहकारी बैंक — 1974)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SEWA (Self-Employed Women's Association) was founded by Ela Bhatt in 1972 as a trade union of poor, self-employed women workers.

• The SEWA Bank provides savings, credit and insurance services to women in the informal sector.

NOTE

• SEWA is a landmark organisation in India's women's empowerment and cooperative movement; Ela Bhatt received the Padma Bhushan and the Ramon Magsaysay Award.

question: In 1973, the first female high court judge of India Anna Chandy published her autobiography __________ in Malayalam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atmakatha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anna Chandy, the first female judge (and later High Court judge) of India, published her autobiography titled "Atmakatha" in Malayalam in 1973. (अन्ना चांडी की आत्मकथा — 'आत्मकथा')

• She became a judge in the Kerala High Court in 1959 and is regarded as one of the first female judges in the Commonwealth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Anna Chandy was also a pioneer of women's rights in India and campaigned for women's employment.

• The other titles are cricketers' books: "The Test of My Life" (Yuvraj Singh), "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "The Race of My Life" (Milkha Singh).

NOTE

• India's first female Supreme Court judge was Justice Fathima Beevi (1989).

question: Kathakali, one of the classical dance forms, is performed primarily in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form performed primarily in the state of Kerala. It is famous for its elaborate costumes, huge headgear, vivid facial make-up (especially green "Pacha") and dramatic storytelling from the epics. (कथकली — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathakali combines dance, music, acting and elaborate mime; the themes are usually drawn from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• Another famous classical dance of Kerala is Mohiniyattam (the "dance of the enchantress").

NOTE

• Classical dances by state: Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Kathak (North India), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Where was the India House established to work for India's liberation from British possession?
solution_text:
The correct answer is London.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "India House" was established in London in 1905 by Shyamji Krishna Varma as a centre for Indian nationalist and revolutionary activities to work for India's freedom from British rule. (इंडिया हाउस — लंदन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India House became a hub for revolutionaries such as V. D. Savarkar, Madan Lal Dhingra, Madam Bhikaji Cama and V. V. S. Aiyar.

• Shyamji Krishna Varma also started the journal "The Indian Sociologist".

NOTE

• Related revolutionary centres abroad: the Ghadar Party (San Francisco, 1913, by Lala Har Dayal & Sohan Singh Bhakna) and the Berlin Committee (Germany). Madam Cama unfurled an early version of the Indian flag at Stuttgart (1907).

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is added by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cooperative Societies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 gave constitutional status to cooperative societies. It:

◦ made the right to form cooperative societies a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(c);

◦ added Article 43B in the Directive Principles (promotion of cooperative societies);

◦ added a new Part IX-B (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT) on cooperative societies. (सहकारी समितियाँ — 97वाँ संशोधन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Ministry of Cooperation was created by the Government of India in 2021 ("Sahakar se Samriddhi").

NOTE

• Other important amendments: 73rd & 74th (1992) — Panchayati Raj and Municipalities; 42nd (1976) — "mini constitution"; 44th (1978); 101st (2016) — GST.

question: Which of the following languages was used by the Sangam poets for composing the texts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sangam literature was composed in the Tamil language, in the ancient assemblies (Sangams) of Tamil poets held in the Madurai region of South India (roughly 300 BCE–300 CE). (संगम साहित्य — तमिल भाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Famous Sangam works include the Tolkappiyam (a work on grammar and poetics) and the anthologies Ettuthogai (Eight Anthologies) and Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls).

• The Sangam age describes the rule of the three Tamil dynasties — the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas.

NOTE

• Tamil is a classical language of India and one of the oldest living languages in the world. Sangam texts are a key source for early South Indian history.

question: Sedimentary rocks are formed by the process of deposition and compaction of fragments of rocks of various sizes. This process is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is lithification.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lithification" is the process by which loose sediments are compacted and cemented together to form solid sedimentary rock. (शिलीभवन / लिथिफिकेशन)

◦ It involves compaction (pressure from overlying layers) and cementation (minerals binding the particles).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Weathering is the breaking down of rocks at the Earth's surface; erosion transports the fragments, which are then deposited and lithified.

• Sedimentary rocks (e.g., sandstone, limestone, shale) often contain fossils and are formed in layers (strata).

NOTE

• The three rock types: Igneous (from cooled magma/lava), Sedimentary (from deposited sediments) and Metamorphic (from heat/pressure changing existing rocks). A "laccolith" is an intrusive igneous landform, not a process.

question: Who received 'Sangeet Natak Akademi' award 2022 for his/her contribution in the field of Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nalini and Kamalini Asthana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kathak dancers Nalini and Kamalini Asthana (the "Asthana sisters") received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2022 for their contribution to Kathak. (कथक — नलिनी एवं कमलिनी अस्थाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama), set up in 1952, is India's apex body for the performing arts.

• The Asthana sisters were also honoured with the Padma Shri (2022) for Kathak.

NOTE

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dances, mainly of North India, known for fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling (abhinaya). Its major gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

question: The religious festival, 'Easter' is celebrated by which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Christian community.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Easter" is an important festival of the Christian community, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, three days after his crucifixion (Good Friday). (ईस्टर — ईसाई समुदाय)

• It is usually celebrated in March or April, on the first Sunday after the full moon following the spring equinox.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 40-day period of Lent precedes Easter; Good Friday marks the crucifixion, and Easter Sunday the resurrection.

• Other Christian festivals: Christmas (birth of Jesus, 25 December) and Palm Sunday.

NOTE

• Festivals by community for SSC: Eid (Muslim), Navroz (Parsi), Paryushana/Mahavir Jayanti (Jain), Buddha Purnima (Buddhist), Baisakhi/Guru Nanak Jayanti (Sikh).

question: The elliptical shapes in temple architecture in Dravidian style are known by which of the given terms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gajaprishta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Dravidian temple architecture, the elliptical or apsidal (elephant-back shaped) plan/shape of a shrine is called "Gajaprishta" — literally meaning "elephant's back". (गजपृष्ठ — हाथी की पीठ जैसी आकृति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Common temple plan shapes: Chatura (square), Ayatasra (rectangular), Vritta (circular), Vrittayata (elliptical) and Gajaprishta (apsidal/elephant-backed).

• "Nasi" refers to the arch-like projections/dormer windows on the temple tower.

NOTE

• The Dravidian (South Indian) style features a pyramidal vimana over the sanctum and a gopuram (gateway tower). The Nagara (North Indian) style features a curvilinear shikhara.

question: In which year did Roshan Mistry become the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal when she took the silver in the 100-m sprint?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951, Asian Games.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Roshan Mistry became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal, taking the silver in the 100-metre sprint at the first Asian Games, held in New Delhi in 1951. (1951 एशियाई खेल — रोशन मिस्त्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first Asian Games (1951) were hosted by India in New Delhi, at the National Stadium, with about 11 participating nations.

• The Asian Games are held every four years and organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

NOTE

• India also hosted the Asian Games in 1982 (New Delhi). The mascot of the 1982 Games was "Appu" the elephant.

question: What is the meaning of the term 'drop shot' in tennis?
option_2: A shot that hits the lines on the court
option_4: A shot played softly and close to the net
solution_text:
The correct answer is A shot played softly and close to the net.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis (and badminton), a "drop shot" is a soft, delicate shot played so that the ball just clears the net and drops close to it, forcing the opponent (usually standing far back) to rush forward. (ड्रॉप शॉट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A powerful overhead shot is a "smash"; a hard, fast serve is an "ace" (if unreturnable); a shot down the side is a "passing shot".

• The drop shot relies on touch and placement rather than power.

NOTE

• Common tennis terms: ace, deuce (40-40), love (zero), fault, let, volley, lob, smash, rally, break point. The four Grand Slams are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.

question: Indian classical vocalist and Padma Vibhushan awardee Kishori Amonkar belongs to which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Hindustani classical vocalist Kishori Amonkar belonged to the Jaipur (Jaipur-Atrauli) gharana. She was the daughter and disciple of the noted vocalist Mogubai Kurdikar. (किशोरी अमोनकर — जयपुर घराना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kishori Amonkar was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1987) and the Padma Vibhushan (2002), and was known for her mastery of khayal and thumri.

• The Jaipur-Atrauli gharana was founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan and is known for complex, intricate ragas.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Kirana, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala and Mewati (associated with Pandit Jasraj).

question: Which of the following organisations was established in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prarthana Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Prarthana Samaj ("Prayer Society") was founded in 1867 in Bombay (Mumbai) by Atmaram Pandurang. It was a socio-religious reform movement that worked against caste restrictions, child marriage and for widow remarriage and women's education. (प्रार्थना समाज — आत्माराम पांडुरंग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Prominent leaders associated with it were Justice M. G. Ranade and R. G. Bhandarkar.

• It was influenced by the Brahmo Samaj of Bengal (Keshab Chandra Sen inspired its founding).

NOTE

• Related reform bodies: Satya Shodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule, 1873), Arya Samaj (Dayananda Saraswati, 1875), Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828), Veda Samaj (South India).

question: Which of the following location has NOT been selected for setting up the seven PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Park for the textile sector announced by the Government of India in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the PM MITRA (Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) Parks scheme, seven parks were announced in March 2023, and West Bengal was NOT among the selected states. (पीएम मित्र पार्क — पश्चिम बंगाल शामिल नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The seven PM MITRA Parks were sanctioned in: Tamil Nadu (Virudhunagar), Telangana (Warangal), Karnataka, Maharashtra (Amravati), Gujarat (Navsari), Madhya Pradesh (Dhar) and Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow/Hardoi).

• The scheme, inspired by the 5F vision — Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign — aims to build integrated, world-class textile infrastructure.

NOTE

• India is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of textiles and cotton; the textile sector is a major source of employment.

question: Which of the following is a NOT a natural fibre crop grown in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Polyester.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Polyester" is a synthetic (man-made) fibre, produced from petrochemicals — it is NOT a natural fibre crop. (पॉलिएस्टर — कृत्रिम रेशा)

• Cotton, hemp and jute are all natural plant fibres grown as crops.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Natural fibres are of plant origin (cotton, jute, hemp, flax/linen) or animal origin (silk, wool).

• Jute is called the "golden fibre"; West Bengal is its leading producer. Cotton grows best in black (regur) soil, mainly in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Telangana.

NOTE

• Examples of synthetic fibres: polyester, nylon, rayon (semi-synthetic), acrylic. They are durable and wrinkle-resistant but less breathable than natural fibres.

question: What is denatured alcohol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol mixed with little methanol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Denatured alcohol" is ethanol (drinking alcohol) made unfit for drinking by adding a small amount of toxic substances such as methanol (and sometimes pyridine or dyes). (विकृत/डिनेचर्ड अल्कोहल)

• This is done so that industrial alcohol can be used tax-free without the risk of it being consumed as a beverage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Methanol is poisonous — it can cause blindness or death if consumed, which is why it is added to denature ethanol.

• Denatured alcohol is used as a solvent, fuel (spirit lamps), and in industry, but not for drinking.

NOTE

• Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is the alcohol in alcoholic drinks; Methanol (CH₃OH), also called "wood spirit", is highly toxic. Adding methanol to ethanol makes it "denatured".

question: Who was appointed as the governor of Bengal by Sultan Balban after the revolt and subsequent death of Tughril Beg?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bughra Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After crushing the revolt of Tughril Beg (Tughril Khan), the governor of Bengal who had rebelled, Sultan Ghiyasuddin Balban appointed his own son Bughra Khan (Nasiruddin Bughra Khan) as the governor of Bengal. (बलबन — बुगरा खान बंगाल का गवर्नर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Balban (r. 1266–1287) of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty was a strong ruler who restored the prestige of the Sultanate. He introduced the Persian court customs Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet) of the Sultan.

• He propounded the theory of the kingship of "Zill-i-Ilahi" (Shadow of God) and maintained a strong spy system and army.

NOTE

• Balban is famous for his policy of "Blood and Iron" to suppress revolts and Mongol threats. He also created the Diwan-i-Arz (military department).
